They are to bring to the Lord in Jerusalem the offering that I and my friends vowed, and all the gold and silver found in the land of Babylon for the Lord who is in Jerusalem.
Whatever you wish to do with that gold and silver together with your companion, do according to the will of your God.
Their elders, each from their own towns, according to the jurisdictions of their territories, who go up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
From [?] Moab: Eliehoenai and Zerahiah, and with him 200 men.
The king gave him honor because he had found favor in his sight, and appointed him over everything.
And from the descendants of Astath: Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men.
The Israelites went up, along with the priests, the Levites, and the priests who sang psalms [?], and [?] priests.
They and their sons married their daughters, and the holy offspring were mixed with the foreign peoples of the land. Their leaders and rulers took the lead in committing this sin.
So that they may honor our temple and build a wall for Zion; and they have given us strength in Judah and Jerusalem.
And now we are before you in our sin, though because of this we are not worthy to stand before you.
This is the Synodos of Clement, written by Peter, the disciple and chief of the apostles, who spoke about our Lord Jesus Christ.

My son, forgive so that you may be forgiven, and do not judge so that you may not be judged. If you have been entrusted with authority appointed by God and judge people, judge with justice and uprightness, as our law declares. Fight with an iron sword against unbelievers and rebels who do not believe in Christ, and sharpen your sword for the perfect faith. Do not show partiality or accept bribes in judgment. Let the rich and the poor be alike before you.

Have mercy on the orphan and provide for the widow. Protect the virgins and strengthen them. Do not give Satan a way to attack you, but drive away his accursed power through fasting, prayer, and keeping watch at night. Let almsgiving be your distinguishing sign, your house, and your dwelling. Protect the children of baptism and the faith.
Do not accept the profession of faith of a man who has not been baptized.

If you see a poor priest, help him by giving him alms, and do not leave him to [?] among the foolish people. Do likewise for all the messengers of God. If you have a blessing, give it to the children of baptism.

Devote yourself earnestly to building churches, monasteries, and convents, which are a dwelling for those oppressed in the world and for the poor. Build houses of God with bright lights, such as wax candles and lamps. Whoever does this, God will approve his deeds and his final outcome.
Fast on Wednesday and Friday all the days of your life.

Let Sunday be a festival. No work is to be done on it except reading the Scriptures concerning the Godhead. Whoever transgresses this is excommunicated and cursed by the three names of God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

Do not drive a poor person away from the door of your dwelling. Do not mock him, reject him, or belittle him. Rather, let your generosity of heart lead you to comfort him and make him glad, so that God may make you glad. Seat him with you at your table, and give him drink from the cup from which you drink. Do not boast over him, for King Nebuchadnezzar boasted and was destroyed, and the wrath of God overtook him.

Do not exalt yourself before a king or act for show in his house. Do not boast over him about your good deeds. Rather, when you do every good deed and fulfill every commandment, say, ‘I am a worthless servant,’ as our Lord said in the book of life, for you will not be saved by the abundance of your evil deeds.
Do not accumulate gold and silver except what you distribute for the benefit of believers.
Clement said, on the authority of Peter, chief of the apostles and disciple of our Lord Christ:

Give abundant peace to the children of the faithful, and praise the upright priest who knows God and acts according to his law. Beware of Satan’s deception, for he deceived Simon the sorcerer after he became a disciple of my brother Philip and after many divine miracles had appeared through his hands. The cause of his error was that he sought priestly ordination and the gift of the Holy Spirit from me through scheming. Our Lord told me that he was deceitful and a thief, and I drove him away from me. This led to his destruction.
My son, honor the elders, hold them in esteem, and listen to their words. Do not ridicule anyone because of his sin, but rebuke him, instruct him, and gently turn him toward the fear of God.
Instruct kings in righteousness and rebuke them for their evil conduct. Do not neglect God’s holy gifts on any day, for offering the sacrifice prevents [?].

Commemorate the dead on the third day, the seventh, the twelfth, the thirtieth, the fortieth, and the sixtieth. Know, my son, that on the fortieth day after the deceased’s passing, the soul of a baptized sinner stands before Christ. He is repaid according to his conduct, and they punish him according to what he has done.

Anoint anyone who desires baptism with the oil of gladness before you baptize him in water. After baptism, seal him with the divine oil that I gave you. This is the oil of chrism, through which everything is brought to completion. Let the faithful stand on their feet to listen to the holy, divine Scriptures.
Do not receive the holy gifts without having purified yourself and fasted.
Pray in the morning, at the third hour of the day, and in the evening, for these three prayers are required of all priests. Let the laypeople pray at dawn and in the evening.

Those who are able and seek a greater measure of divine grace should pray as we prescribed in the Book of Church Order. For Christ my God taught me, and I tell you, my son Clement, that they ought to pray at the first hour of the day, at the third hour, at the sixth hour, at the ninth hour, in the evening, at bedtime, and at midnight.
I, Peter, command the faithful to rest from their work and their occupations on the feast days of the martyrs.

I warn them against wicked drunkenness, attending theatrical performances, and singing in the streets. They must not eat what an unbaptized person has slaughtered, for God has abolished the sacrifices of the Jews and of foreign nations.
He said to me, “My son Clement, do not baptize anyone for bribes or for a fixed payment for baptism.

We command them not to eat the unleavened bread of the Jews or anything from their sacrifices. They must not give their own in marriage to them or marry anyone from among them. Anyone among them who believes and is baptized must stand at the church door for forty days and eat nothing but dry bread.

If he does this, let him approach God’s sanctuary after they have tested his faith, and let them pierce his ear. Let them feed him the offering of the faithful, and especially the flesh of the holy animal that appeared to me in a shining cloth that descended upon me in the city of Joppa, for it is holy among all animals.

When you wish to sleep, believer, make the sign of the cross over your face and your whole body. If you wish to set out on a journey, receive a blessing from the bones of the martyrs before you depart.

Priest, do not offer fat or flesh on the altar. Do not place anything on the altar except pure bread of fine flour, of which he said, “It is my body,” for God called it heavenly bread; and nothing from the [?] except grape juice, for God called it the water of life; and fresh ears from the wheat crop when it ripens. You are not permitted to bring anything else as an offering. A priest must not offer wine on the altar without adding water, for our Lord Christ said, “I am the water of life.”

Concerning the observance of festivals. Keep a festival during the days of Christ’s sufferings, his sorrow, and his crucifixion. During those days, join sorrow and joy together. Let there be sorrow because of his endurance in affliction, and joy because your salvation comes through Christ’s suffering.
The feast of Easter is greater and more honored than all the festivals. Let there be no sorrow in it, but only joy.
Commemorate your dead in the liturgy at all times, for this greatly benefits them and brings them near to our Lord Christ.
Celebrate the feast of Easter at its completion, on the Sunday that comes after Passover. This is the day of the resurrection of our Lord Christ from the tomb.

Celebrate a feast seven days after his resurrection, on New Sunday, for on that day he came to us, the assembly of the Twelve, after his resurrection from the dead, while we were gathered in the upper room in Zion with the doors shut. On that day Thomas found him and touched with his hand the place of the spear wound in the side of our Lord Christ and the places of the nails, until he burned the tips of his fingers. Our God renewed them and restored them to life, and said to him, “Do not doubt, Thomas, but believe.”

Celebrate the feast of his ascension into heaven and the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon us apostles. For he descended from heaven upon our mouths like tongues of fire and taught us things that we did not know, had not heard before then, and had not understood. This was after Christ’s ascension into heaven, from which he had not departed, in a chariot of light from the Mount of Olives, forty days after his resurrection.
Whoever accepts bribes for baptism at a fixed price is excommunicated and cursed by my mouth—I, Peter, the least of the apostles. Let his portion be with Simon the sorcerer and Judas the wicked.

Celebrate a feast at the time of her annunciation, for the Gentiles celebrated it before you as a feast for their gods. But you are to make it a feast for the Mother of Light, as the chosen man of God, Paul, commanded.
Celebrate all the feasts that we commanded you in the Book of Church Order.

Know, my son, concerning incense with [?], for [?] is the great incense that they burn before God. Our Lady, the Mother of Light, told me and gave me some of it. It is what the Magi brought as a gift. Myrrh, however, is to be used for embalming the bodies of priests so that they do not decay. They are not to bury them in the earth, but halfway above the earth.
My son, keep my commandment as Joshua son of Nun kept the commandment of my brother Moses.

Concerning the consecration of the tabot. Consecrate every tabot of the law and seal it with the seal of God, which is chrism, the oil of gladness. Seven priests are to be with you when you consecrate it, for they are our successors. Seal the tabots and the altars with the seal of God, so that the glory of God may be found wherever they celebrate the consecration upon them. Seal everyone who is baptized with this holy oil. Through it they will receive priesthood and kingship, and prophecy will abound through the anointing with chrism and through its glory.

If anyone seals himself with this holy oil, which I, Peter, the least of the apostles, give you, without being sealed by a priest authorized to do so, let them seize him. I have authorized them to kill him.

If anyone drinks some of it for his healing, let him be banished to a place from which he will not return. Any layperson who dares to carry it without knowing is to be expelled from the church of God for seven years.
If he carries it knowingly, let them strike him with one hundred and fifty-three lashes, and let him remain outside the church for ten years.
If a priest anoints someone who has not been baptized with this oil, let him be removed from his office.
If a priest takes this oil to someone who is not a priest, let him be removed from his office.

My son, do not sell the gift of priesthood and the grace of the Holy Spirit for a price. Do not bargain over the priesthood, and do not accept payment for it, either before you give the blessing or afterward, except as a blessing.
If a priest carries this oil, let him recite the psalm of David the prophet, who prophesied concerning this oil, until he sets it down from his hands.
If anyone takes the priesthood for himself without receiving it from the chief priest, let him be expelled from the church of God.

Concerning the order of the altar. Let them consecrate the offering upon an altar sealed with chrism, on the first occasion when the chief priests and priests assemble together with all the deacons, so that there may be honor and joy. Likewise on Sabbaths and feast days. Let them read the Gospel of John over the altar, for he is the one who speaks of the Godhead.

In every sanctuary there are to be two altars: one that they carry from place to place, like the stone of the children of Israel in the wilderness, which they carried from place to place; and another that they do not move from its place.

If the altar that is not moved is broken, or people move it from the place where it was consecrated, know that its holiness has departed from it, just as the holiness of the children of Israel departed from his offspring. They must consecrate it again.

If one of the faithful is taken captive, or goes and joins the Gentiles, eats their food, has contact with them and they with him, and is defiled by them, and then returns to his country from his captivity, they must baptize him again.

If a layperson enters the holy altar of God during the consecration, seeking greater honor than his fellow, they must excommunicate him. He must stand outside the church for seven years and show people his repentance.

If a layperson insults a priest or curses him, he must be banished from the cities of God and his churches to the land of rebels. If he seeks refuge at the altar of God and takes hold of the vestments, the priest must prescribe twelve years of fasting for him and perform over him the anointing for the forgiveness of sins.

If a man or woman among the faithful eats any of what is offered, that person must be banished from the church of God until death, if this was done out of contempt. If it was done without knowledge, that person must fast for twelve full years. They must give the church double that person's possessions. That person must not give orders but must be put to work.

If a man among the faithful enters inside the curtain of the altar, stretches out his hand against a priest, and strikes him, they must cut off his hand for his insolence toward the priesthood of God.

Whoever gives or receives bribes for the priesthood has no priesthood. He is excommunicated by me, Peter, with the excommunication with which I excommunicated Simon the sorcerer. Let his portion be with Judas the rebellious, and let his soul be far from the presence of God, as the devil is far from his former rank.
If a man among the faithful has committed many sins and wishes to refrain from them, he must disclose them to the priests and to those learned in the Scriptures of God.

Concerning priestly vestments. Priestly vestments must be different from the clothing of laypeople. The priest's garment should be loose, without folds, and its [?] should be wide at the bottom. His garment must be like this, and its upper part must be rounded, for this represents the binding of the feet of our Lord Christ. He must uncover his hands with a cord.

The priest must wear a cloth like a neckband over his shoulders, for it represents the cord they placed around the neck of our Lord Christ when they dragged him to Pilate's courtyard. His belt must be broad and made of leather.
The priest must read the Psalms of David by day and the Praises of the Prophets by night, for through this they will be girded with two swords.

I tell you, my son Clement, and those who share your rank, to judge between the faithful and give them appropriate commands according to what the Holy Spirit has shown you, who brings [?] to completion. Whoever rebels and leads others astray is cursed until the day of judgment, when he will stand before Christ.
Know, my son, that everything I have commanded you, I have commanded you by God's command.
With his own hand he wrote this command for me and gave it to me on the Mount of Olives on the day of his ascension into his glory. Amen.
My son, forgive whoever sins against you seventy times seven, as our Lord commanded in the holy Gospel.

Receive whoever repents of his sin. Have mercy on whoever has sinned, take him by the hand and raise him up, and admonish him. Visit the sick, go to the prisoners, feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, and clothe the naked.

Be steadfast in the faith and struggle for it with the uprightness that is fitting. Listen to the holy Scriptures of God, for those who hold firmly to the faith and struggle for it will inherit the kingdom of heaven.
How can I alone bear your trouble, your affairs, and your disputes?

Where, then, are we to go up? Your brothers discouraged your hearts and told you, ‘The people are great and numerous, and stronger than we are. Their cities are large, with fortifications reaching up to heaven. We also saw the children of giants there.’
The Lord was angry with me also because of you, and he told me, ‘You too shall not enter there.’
But you turned back and traveled into the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.
The Amorites who lived on that mountain came out to meet you, fell upon you, pursued you, and stung you like bees. They struck you down from Seir to Hormah.
Moses began to declare this law and said:
At that time I said to you, ‘I cannot bear you alone.’
I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me during those days too, and the Lord spared you and did not destroy you.
Look, heaven, the heaven of heavens, the earth, and everything in it belong to the Lord your God.
I will write on these tablets all the words that were on the earlier tablets you broke. Put them in the ark.
Fear the Lord your God, worship him alone, follow him, and swear by his name.
Love the Lord your God and keep his law, statutes, commandments, and judgments throughout all the days of your life.
And the Lord will become angry with you and shut the sky, so that no rain comes and the earth does not yield its fruit, and you will quickly perish from the blessed land that the Lord has given you.
And if you faithfully obey every commandment that I give you today, carrying them out, loving the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, and following him;
So that your days may be long in the land that the Lord swore to give to your fathers and their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And when the Lord your God destroys before you the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you dispossess them and live in their land;
And you must not do this to the Lord your God.

Gather all its goods into its streets and burn the city with fire, together with all its goods. Treat the whole city in this way before the Lord your God. No one shall ever live in it, and it shall not be rebuilt.
And his sign or wonder that he told you about comes to pass, while he says, “Come, let us go and worship gods that you do not know”;
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, listen to his voice, and take refuge in him.
But do not eat anything that has no fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
And these are the birds you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the sea eagle;
And this is what you may eat from the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
And remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. For this reason I command you to do this.
And if there is someone impoverished among your brothers in one of your towns that the Lord your God has given you, do not turn your heart away or close your hand against giving to your brother.
Instead, open your hand wide and give your brother what he asks of you, from what he asks of you.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God has chosen: at the festival of the law of Hallelujah, at the festival of the Sabbath, and at the festival of Booths. Do not come before the Lord your God empty-handed.

Do not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of suffering, because you came out of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
And it shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn the way of the Lord his God, keep all his commandments, and carry out his judgments;

And if a matter of judgment is too difficult for you, between blood and blood, between cleanness and purification, or between injury and injury—matters of judgment within your towns—you shall rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be named there.
For those nations that you are dispossessing practice divination and listen to oracles, but it is not to be so with you.
And he shall serve in the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord.
And others shall hear and be afraid, and shall not again do this evil thing among you.
And you shall show him no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.
The Emim formerly lived in it, a very great people, strong like those in [?].
And when all those fighting men had fallen and died from among the people,
Sell me food for my gold, so that I may eat, and sell me water for my gold, so that I may drink. I will only pass through on foot.
Except for their livestock, which we took as spoil for ourselves; and we plundered the cities we captured.
Command the people and tell them, ‘Look, you are passing through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will be very afraid of you.’

And the officers shall say to the people, “If there is a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man dedicate his house.”
Afterward, if you do not want her, you shall let her go free. You must not sell her for gold or deal treacherously with her, since you married her.
If a man has a rebellious and insolent son who does not obey his father or his mother, and they discipline him but he does not listen to them;
And the elders of that city shall bring the heifer to a rugged valley that has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall cut the heifer’s tendons.
Forgive your people Israel, Lord, whom you redeemed from the land of Egypt, so that guilt for taking a life may not rest upon your people Israel. And they will be forgiven for that life.
If you see your neighbor’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not ignore them. Help him lift it up.
If you come upon a bird’s brood before you on the road, in any tree or on the ground, whether chicks or eggs, do not take the mother with her young.
Take a wooden implement with you in your belt. When you sit down, dig a hole, then get up and cover your excrement.
Do not bring the earnings of prostitution or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God for any vow, for both are unclean before the Lord your God.
Do not speak of peace or well-being for them throughout all your days, forever.
Do not take a mill or its upper millstone as a pledge, for it is a means of sustaining life, and it must not be taken as a pledge.
If there is a dispute between people and they come to court to have their case judged, the judges shall acquit the one who is right and condemn the one who is wrong;
Do not keep for yourself a small measure and a large measure.
For the Lord has chosen you today to be his own people, as he said, so that you may keep all his commandments;
You shall say before the Lord your God, “My father left Syria and went down to Egypt. He lived there when they were few in number, and there he became a great nation, very populous and numerous.”
Cursed be anyone who dishonors his father and his mother. And all the people shall say, “Amen and amen.”
You shall build an altar to the Lord your God with stones that have not been hewn.
You shall offer sacrifices of well-being upon them. Eat and be satisfied there, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Moses and the priests said to the Levites and to all Israel, “Be silent and listen, Israel. On this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.”
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be left to you, for they will be taken away and led into captivity.
It will be a sign and a wonder upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart when you had an abundance of everything.
The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, like an eagle swooping down—a nation whose speech you do not understand;
A nation with a fierce face, which does not respect the elderly or show mercy to the young;
The woman among you who is delicate and weak, who [?] her feet to walk on the ground because she is delicate and weak, will look begrudgingly at the husband in her embrace, her son, and her daughter.
If you do not obey and carry out all the words of this law written in this book, so that you fear this honored and glorious name, that of the Lord your God.
He will bring back upon them all those evil diseases of Egypt which you did not fear (from which you did not fear) when confronted with them, and they will cling to you.
The Lord will bring upon you every disease and every plague that is not written in this book of the law, until he destroys you and you are wiped out.
So that he may make you his people and may himself be your God, as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Let there be no man or woman, people or tribe, or anyone among you whose heart turns away from the Lord your God and who goes to worship these gods of the nations. Let there be no evil root among you that sprouts and bears poison and bitterness.

The Lord will not be willing to forgive him. Instead, at that time the Lord’s anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse of this covenant written in this book of the law will pursue him. The Lord will erase his name from under heaven.

The later generation, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will speak when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases that the Lord has sent upon it;
But your wives and your children—and I know that you have many livestock—shall remain in your cities, which I gave you,

until the Lord our God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land that the Lord our God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then all of you shall return to your inheritance, which I gave you.
At that time I also commanded Joshua and told him, ‘Your eyes have seen everything the Lord did to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to every kingdom into which you go.’

O Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your strength and your power, the strength of your hand and the greatness of your arm. What god is there in heaven or on earth who does what you have done?

For I will bring them into the blessed land that I swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey. When they have eaten and are satisfied, they will grow fat and turn to other gods and worship them. They will provoke me and abandon my covenant.
Moses commanded Joshua and said to him, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land that the Lord swore to their fathers, and he will be with you.”
For I know your rebelliousness and your stubborn neck. Even while I am still alive today, you have rebelled against the Lord. How much more will you do so after my death!
For the Lord will judge his people and plead the cause of his servants, because he sees that they have wasted away and perished and have been abandoned where they are.

Let all the heavens rejoice together, and let all the angels of God bow down to him. Let the nations rejoice with their peoples, and let all the children of God say, “He is mighty!” For he will avenge the blood of his children. He will take vengeance and repay his adversaries with vengeance, and he will repay those who hate him. The Lord will cleanse the land for his people.
And when Moses had finished speaking to all Israel;
Die on the mountain that you ascend there, and join your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before he died.
He said, “The Lord came from Sinai and also appeared in Seir. He rested on Mount Paran with the myriads of Kadesh, those at his right, his angels, and those with him.”
Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died, and his eyes had neither grown dim nor deteriorated.
in the likeness of any animal on the earth, or in the likeness of any winged bird that flies beneath heaven;
Do not add to the word that I command you today, and do not take anything away from it, so that you may keep all the commandments of the Lord your God.
But the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, so that you would be his own people, as you are to this day.
The Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations into which the Lord brings you.
Know today that the Lord God is the Lord in heaven above and on earth below, and there is no other besides him.
Bezer in the wilderness, in the open country, for Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead for Gad; and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.
Moses called all Israel and said to them, ‘Listen, Israel, to all the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing today, on this day. Learn to carry them out and keep them.’

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any of your work, neither you nor your son nor your daughter nor your male servant nor your female servant nor your ox nor your donkey nor any of your livestock nor the foreigner within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.
Do not go to another man's wife. Do not kill anyone. Do not steal. Do not be a false witness against your neighbor. Do not falsify testimony.

These are the words the Lord spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain, from the midst of fire, darkness, storm, and thick cloud, with a loud voice. He added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets, and the Lord gave them to me.
For what mortal has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of fire, as we have, and remained alive?
But you, stand beside me. I will tell you all my commandments, statutes, and laws, which you are to teach them so that they may follow them in the land I am giving them as their inheritance.
Along the whole path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow, so that things may go well for you, that you may have rest, and that your days may be long in the land you will inherit.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the nations around you.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you tested him on the day of testing.
Do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God, so that things may go well for you and you may enter and inherit the blessed land that the Lord swore to your fathers.
The Lord sent great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his household, before our eyes.
He will repay those who hate him to their faces and destroy them. He will not delay the destruction of those who hate him, but will confront them directly.
Keep all his commandments, statutes, and laws that I command you today, and carry them out.
Do not bring an unclean thing into your house and become accursed like it. Regard it as utterly unclean and utterly detest it, for it is accursed.
For he will turn your son away from me, and your son will worship other gods. The Lord's anger will burn against you, and he will quickly destroy you.
He fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and test you, and to do good to you in your later days.
Keep all the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed with the finger of the Lord. On them were written all the words the Lord spoke to us on the mountain on the day you assembled.

And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, "Go up and take possession of the land I am giving you," you rebelled against the word of the Lord your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
You have been rebellious against the Lord from the day he became known to you.

I prayed to the Lord and said, "Lord, King of the gods, do not destroy your people, your own portion, whom you redeemed by your great power and brought out of Egypt by your great power, your strong hand, and your uplifted arm."
What has he done beyond what has been done, and what has happened beyond what has happened? There is nothing that has been done under the sun.
A generation passes away, and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever.
All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is not filled in its place.
When a fool walks in the folly of his heart and follows his heart's desire, understanding fails him, and everything he thinks is foolish.
I saw slaves on horses and rulers walking on foot like slaves.
The person who moves a stone is hurt by it, and the person who splits wood is injured by it.
Send your bread out upon the surface of the water, for after many days you will find it.
The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it. It will give an account of everything he did to me while he lived in the flesh, whether good or evil.
Moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he taught knowledge to all the people, and examined the arrangement of proverbs.
On the day when the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men are shaken, the women who grind are brought low because they are weak, and those who look through the windows grow dark.
I looked to see wisdom, folly, and madness. Who is the man who will follow after counsel, and every example he made for it? [?]
To the one who sins he gave the task of increasing and gathering wealth, so that he might give it to the good person who stands before God. This too is emptiness and a desire for wind.
I made vegetable gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every kind of tree that bears fruit in its season, and every kind that does not bear fruit.
A time to live and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot what was planted; a time to wound and a time to heal; a time to build and a time to tear down.
A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time for amusement and a time to dance.
If he is strong, the two will stand against him, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
I saw all the living together, those who walk under the sun, with another young man who rises in his place.
Look, there are tears among those who are oppressed, and there is no one to comfort them against those who oppress them by force.
Every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and whom he has empowered to eat from them, take his share, and rejoice in his labor—this too is God's gift.
When you make a vow, do not delay fulfilling it, for that is not his will. Rather, give what you have vowed.
Wisdom helps the wise person more than a thousand rulers who are in the city.
She is far from me, remaining far away and deeply, deeply hidden. Who can find her?
I turned my mind toward understanding, to consider and seek wisdom and reasoning, and to understand the folly of the wicked and the mockery of errors.

I find her more bitter than death: the woman who is a trap, whose heart is a net, and whose hands hold bonds. The person who is good before God escapes from her, but the one who sins is caught by her.
There was found within it a wise but poor man, and he saved that city by his wisdom. Yet no one at all remembered that man.
Because the midwives feared God, they built houses.
Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Throw every boy born to the Hebrews into the Nile, but keep every girl alive.”
Another king rose to power over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, so that my signs may come upon them together.”
And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and darkness and dust covered the whole land of Egypt for three days.
And Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, “Go and serve the Lord your God, but leave your sheep and cattle behind. You may take your possessions with you.”

Our livestock must also go with us, and we will leave nothing behind, because we will take some of them to sacrifice to the Lord our God. We do not know what service we must render to the Lord our God until we arrive there.
And they summoned Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh, and he said to them (Pharaoh to Moses and Aaron), “Go and serve the Lord your God. But who exactly are those of you who will go?”
This month shall be the first of the months for you; put it before the other months of the year.

Take a bundle of hyssop and dip it in the blood beside the door. Apply some of that blood beside the door of the house to the lintel and both doorposts. And you must not leave that house until morning.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the law of the Passover: no one of a foreign people may eat of it.”
And on that day the Lord brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt with their forces.
And the Lord said to Moses:
And the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites to turn back and camp opposite Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, toward Baal-zephon. Camp opposite them, beside the sea.”

And they said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in the land of Egypt that you brought us out to kill us in the wilderness? What have you done to us by bringing us out of the land of Egypt?”
The Lord will fight for you, and you must remain silent.
And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them. I will be glorified through Pharaoh and all his army, and all Egypt will know that I am the Lord.

And the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled. Pharaoh’s heart and the hearts of his officials turned against the people, and he said, “What have we done, letting the Israelites go so that they no longer serve us?”
And you led your people whom you redeemed; by your strength you made the remnant of your sanctuary rejoice.
The nations heard and trembled; anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
At that time the chiefs of Edom trembled; shaking seized the messengers of Moab, and all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
Fear and trembling seized them; the strength of your arm was greater than rocks, until your people passed over, Lord, until your people passed over—this people whom you redeemed.
Miriam took the lead and said, “Let us bless the Lord. He is wonderful, wonderful! He threw the horse and its rider into the sea.”
Moses cried out to the Creator, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he showed him righteousness and judgment, and tested him.

“I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘In the evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the Lord, your Creator.’”
They gathered it every morning, each for himself, and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On Friday they gathered a double portion, two omers for each person. All the leaders of the assembly came and told Moses.
Moses said to them, “Eat it today, because today is the Lord’s Sabbath. You will not find it in the wilderness.”
On the seventh day, some of the people went out to gather it, but found none.

Moses said, “In the evening the Lord will give you meat to eat, and in the morning bread until you are satisfied, because the Lord has heard your grumbling—the grumbling with which you grumble against us. And who are we? This grumbling of yours is not against us, but against the Creator.”

Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took an offering and made a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness. Aaron and the leaders of the people of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before the Lord.
Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek judgment from the Lord.”
In the third month after the Israelites left the land of Egypt, on that day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet the Creator, and they reached the mountain.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people not to approach the Lord to look at him, lest many among them fall.”
The priest of Midian had seven daughters, who tended their father’s sheep. When they came, they drew [?] until they filled the troughs to water their father’s sheep.
He said to his daughters, “Where is he? Why did you leave the man like that? Call him so that he may eat some food.”
When they could no longer hide him, his mother took a basket and coated it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child inside it and placed it among the reeds beside the Nile.
His sister watched from a distance to find out what would happen to him.
The child’s sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Would you like me to call a nursing woman from among the Hebrew women to nurse this child for you?”
Honor your father and your mother, so that righteousness may be yours. You will have many days in the righteous land that the Lord God gives you.
Do not worship gods of silver, and do not worship gods of gold. Do not make such gods for yourselves.
If someone has stolen among the Israelites, and [?] your companion [?] you bring back [?], whoever you find shall be sentenced to death.
If you acquire a Jewish slave, keep him for seven years, and in the seventh year set him free without payment.
If someone wounds his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies, the one who inflicted the wound shall surely be put to death.
If two men fight and injure a pregnant woman, and she miscarries and there is no human form, they shall fine him if her husband agrees to a settlement, according to his demand.
If she miscarries when it is formed, he shall pay life for life.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
If he breaks a molar or tooth of his male or female slave, he shall set them free in compensation for their tooth.
Whether it is a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty pieces of silver to the slave’s owner in either case, and his ox shall be stoned.
Do not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, because you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall be holy people to me. Do not eat the flesh of an animal killed by a wild beast; throw it to the dogs.
For seven years sow your fields and gather your harvest.
But in every seventh year leave it to rest, so that the poor of your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what remains. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.
Observe everything I have said. Do not mention the names of gods, and do not speak them with your mouths.
Three times every male shall appear before me, the Lord your God.
Bring the first fruits of your fields into the house of the Lord your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
I will not drive them out in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild animals of the land do not multiply against you.
Keep away from every unjust judgment. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous, and do not spare the guilty.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you stone tablets bearing the law and the commandment that I have written, so that you may instruct them.”
The splendor of the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Moses rose early in the morning and built an altar beside the mountain, and twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Insert its poles into those four rings on the supports of the ark, as carrying poles for the ark by which they will carry it.
Make a covering of pure gold to fit above it, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Place the covering on top of the ark, and put inside the ark the commandment that I will give you.
Make its dishes, its bowls, its pouring vessels, and its measuring vessels with which you will pour. Make them of pure gold.
Place bread on the table before me continually.
For the shaft of the lampstand, make four cups, with its flowers and its rounded tops.
Fashion what is behind it and its arrangement [?] from pure gold.
Make fifty loops along the edge of one curtain, at the middle where the curtains are joined. Make fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain, where it is joined to the first.
Each upright shall be ten cubits high and one and a half cubits wide.
Make forty silver sockets for the twenty uprights: two sockets for one upright, for its two faces, and two sockets for another upright, for its two faces.
Five curtains shall be joined, one joined to another, and five curtains shall be linked to one another.
On the other side, the curtain shall stand fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.
Make for it pans for the sacrifices, its shovels, its bowls, its meat forks, and its fire pans. Make them all of bronze.
Its boards shall be hollow. Make it that way, just as I showed you on the mountain; make it that way.
With the work of a skilled craftsman, engrave both stones with the names of the sons of Israel, as a seal is engraved.
And you shall make wild animals of the earth from pure gold.
And it shall be set with settings, with its stones in four rows. A row of stones shall be made of sardius, topaz, and emerald: one row.
And you shall place it opposite where the hooks of its chain project [judgment], on both sides, from its shoulder pieces; and you shall place it from the judgment [?].

And above it and below it you shall make things like pomegranate fruit, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, below the woven garment, all around it. Join it [?] to golden pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
And the golden pomegranates, their bells, and their flowers shall be at the [?] of his garment all around.
And you shall put it on a blue thread, and they shall place it on the serpent, so that it rests at the end of the serpent.
And you shall cut it into its separate pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and place its head among the pieces you have cut.
And you shall offer the whole ram on the altar as an offering to the Lord.
And you shall take it from their hands and offer it on the altar as a pleasing aroma before the Lord. It is an offering to the Lord.
And you shall take the breast of the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and present it as a special offering before the Lord, and it alone shall be your portion.

And it shall be a perpetual ordinance for Aaron and his sons among the Israelites, because this is a special offering. It shall be a special offering from the Israelites, from the sacrifices they offer for their deliverance, a special offering to the Lord.
And you shall take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might be called upon by them and be their God.
Moses said to God, “Look, I will go to the Israelites and tell them, ‘The God of your ancestors has sent me to you.’ If they ask me his name, what shall I tell them?”
And you shall overlay it with pure gold—its base, its sides all around, and its horns—and you shall make a gold molding around it.
And the oil used for anointing and the incense burned for the sanctuary. And they shall make everything I command you.
And keep my Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Whoever profanes it shall certainly be put to death. Whoever does work on it—that person shall be cut off from their people.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall certainly [?] be put to death.
Look, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
And I have provided Eliab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. And I have given understanding to everyone skilled in heart, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
And now leave me alone, and in my anger and wrath I will destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.

And he said to them, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Let each man carry his sword. Go from gate to gate through the camp, and let each man kill his brother, let each man kill his fellow, and let each man kill his neighbor.”
And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them, and three thousand men from among the people fell at that time.
And all the people took off the earrings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
And on the next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. And now I will go up to the Lord to obtain forgiveness for your sin.”
And the Lord killed some of the people because they had made the calf that Aaron made for them.
And God said to Moses, “Here is a place beside me, and you shall stand on the rock.”
“Be ready in the morning, and go up Mount Sinai. Stand there before me on the mountaintop.”
“You shall celebrate the Sabbath festival for me when the wheat harvest begins, and the Festival of Booths in the middle of the year.”
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and saw that his face had become radiant, they were afraid to approach him.
And the Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, merciful and compassionate, slow to anger, abundant in mercy, and righteous,

who preserves righteousness and shows mercy to thousands, who forgives wrongdoing, error, and sin, but does not acquit the guilty; who brings the fathers’ sins upon their children and their children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”
And Moses said, “If I have found favor before you, let my Lord go with us, for this people is stubborn. Forgive the sin and guilt of your people, and we will belong to you.”
And the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, and the altar and all its utensils;
and the garments of Aaron the priest, and the garments in which they serve in the sanctuary;
Everyone who had pledged an offering of silver or bronze brought an offering to God. Everyone who had wood that does not decay brought it for all the work needed for the tabernacle.
And all the women whose hearts prompted them skillfully spun the goats’ hair.
They cut the gold leaf and made it into threads to be woven with blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver.
And they made two twisted circlets and two gold rings.

He fastened the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod. They were secured with blue cords and woven into the [?] of the ephod, so that the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as God had commanded Moses.
And they made linen tunics, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons;
And they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more offerings than are needed for the work that God commanded to be done.”
And all the skilled workers who made the sacred garments made them for Aaron the priest, as God had commanded Moses.
And the courtyard on the west side was fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and ten bases.
And the hanging on the south side was fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
And its four pillars had four bronze bases. Their fastenings were of silver, their capitals were covered with silver, and the pillars themselves were covered with silver.
and they made an embroidered curtain for the doorway of the tabernacle, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver, and depicted cherubim on it.
And its five pillars, their rings, their capitals, and their bands they overlaid with gold; and their five bases were of bronze.
And he made carrying poles for the ark and the table and covered them with gold.
Handles by which they grasp it when they lift it.
Moses saw all the work that had been done. They had done it just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Moses blessed them.
One hundred talents for one hundred capitals; one talent for each capital.
The bronze from the offering amounted to four hundred and seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
“Now go, and I will open your mouth and teach you what you must say.”
The Lord said to Moses, “What is this in your hand?” He said, “A staff.”
Zipporah took a razor and cut off her son’s foreskin. She fell at his feet and said, “Let this blood from my son’s circumcision be a substitute for him.”
Aaron told them all the words that God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
He arranged its lamps before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the golden incense altar in the tent of the testimony, in front of the curtain.
You shall put the ark of the testimony in place and screen the ark with the curtain.
You shall place the golden incense altar, on which incense is burned, before the ark of the testimony, and put a curtain at the entrance of the tent of the testimony.
Their taskmasters kept urging them on, saying, “Complete your work each day, just as when we gave you straw.”
They met Moses and Aaron as they were coming out from Pharaoh.
“Go in and tell Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to send the Israelites out of his land.”
These are the messengers, according to their ancestral houses:
The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I have made you a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.”
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded them. Aaron raised his staff and struck the water in the Nile before Pharaoh and his officials, and the water in the Nile became blood.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the Lord says: Let my people go so that they may serve me (in the wilderness).’”
They gathered them into heaps, and the land stank.
When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became hard, and he refused to listen to them, as the Lord had said.
The Lord said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out the staff in your hand and strike the dust of the ground, and gnats will come out upon people and animals throughout the land of Egypt.’”
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought out the frogs. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
And the Lord did so. Dogflies came in great numbers into Pharaoh’s houses, into the houses of his officials, and throughout the land of Egypt. The land was ruined by the dogflies.
We will go three days’ journey into the open country and sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he told us.
But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also and refused to let the people go.
Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh and cried out to the Lord for the destruction of the frogs, as Pharaoh had requested.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let hail fall throughout the land of Egypt, on people, on animals, and on all the vegetation in the land.”
But the wheat and peas were not struck, because they were ripe.
It will become dust throughout the land of Egypt, and it will cause boils that break out on people and animals, on human beings and four-footed creatures throughout the land of Egypt.

When Ezra finished his prayer and confession, weeping as he prayed before the house of the Lord, many men from Israel gathered around him. There was a great assembly, together with their wives and their young people, and the people wept bitterly.
Now praise the Lord, the God of our fathers, and do what is good before him. Separate yourselves from the nations of the land and from the foreign women.
But Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah are with me in this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite help them.

The descendants of the exiles did so. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of their ancestral families, according to their households, all designated by name. They sat down on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
He finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the descendants of the priests, these were found to have married foreign women: from the descendants of Joash son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eleazar, Orem, and Gedaliah.
From Israel, from the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.

But let us make a covenant with our God, and [?] Israel now concerning this, so that they send away their wives together with the children they have borne them. Arise and rebuke them as you wish, according to the commandment of our God, and let them act according to our law.
And from the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluh, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu.
This is what it means: great turmoil will arise from within the body of that kingdom, and it will be shaken toward collapse. Yet it will not fall at that time, but will remain in power.
For those heads of the kingdom are its end.
And he will mercifully redeem the remaining people, those who have survived within my borders, and make them rejoice until the day of judgment arrives, of which I told you before.
How have we sinned against you, and how have we wronged you, that you should leave us and stay in this place?
For you alone remain to us out of all the prophets, like a single cluster of grapes out of all that is gathered, like a lamp in a dark place, and like a harbor for a ship amid a storm.
For we are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten us.
And after this I saw that man come down from that mountain and call to himself many others who hated him.
For they grieve without knowing what is reserved for them in the last days, which have not yet come upon them.
And this is the interpretation of the dream you saw, and for this reason I showed it to you alone.
And on the third day, while I was sitting under a tree.
For I am going away, Lord, and as you commanded me, I will teach the people who are alive now. Who, then, will teach those who are born afterward?
And I went as he commanded me and gathered all the people.
For he who gave you your law at the proper time is a righteous judge.
And the Most High gave wisdom to those five men, and they wrote all this in characters they did not know, in sequence. They stayed there for forty days, and they wrote during the day.
And in the evening they ate food, while I spoke during the day and did not remain silent at night.

And the people of Judah entered their cities, those who had come out with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This was the number of the people of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: 2,172.
And the descendants of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, and the descendants of Hadid and Ono: 725.

And the descendants of the gatekeepers—the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai—139 in all.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, and the descendants of Harhur.
And the descendants of Pahath-moab, those descended from Jeshua and Joab: 2,812.
When the seventh month arrived, Israel was living in their cities. Then the people gathered together in Jerusalem as one person.

They laid the foundation to build the house of the Lord. The priests stood in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, praised the Lord with cymbals as they laid the foundation of the house of the Lord, according to the instruction of David, king of Israel.

Many of the priests, Levites, representatives of their ancestral families, and elders who knew the former house wept loudly when they laid its foundation and saw this house with their own eyes. And many shouted with cries of celebration as they spoke.

They celebrated the Feast of Booths as it was written, and offered the sacrifices in the number prescribed for each day, according to the regulations for the people, at their appointed times, day by day.
The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the descendants of the exiles were building a house for the Lord, the God of Israel.
And now restrain those men so that they do not build that city. From now on, keep watch over them.
Take care not to neglect them in this matter, so that its destruction does not increase and they do not harm the kings.
Then the construction of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was stopped, and it remained suspended until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
We also asked them their names so that we could write to you, so that you might know the names of those men and of their leaders.

They gave us this answer, saying, “We are servants of the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding this house, which was built long ago, many years before. A great king of Israel built it and erected it for them.
But when our ancestors provoked the God of heaven, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He demolished the house and deported the people to Babylon.

And now, if the king wishes, let a search be made in the treasury of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that King Cyrus ordered this house of the Lord in Jerusalem to be built. And, having considered it, lord king, send us what you wish.”
Then King Darius ordered them to open the books of their [?] in the treasury in Babylon.

May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and nations who transgress this decree of mine and who raise their hands to alter and destroy the house of the Lord in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have commanded that they do this and carry it out diligently.
The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the descendants of the exiles celebrated the dedication of the house of the Lord with joy.

They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, because the Lord had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, strengthening their hands for the work on the house of the God of Israel.
The king and his seven counselors gave orders and sent them to examine matters in Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of their God, which is in your hand.
The son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub.
Let everything be done according to the law of the God of heaven. Take care not to harm the house of the God of heaven, so that wrath does not come upon the king’s kingdom and upon his children.
And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of God that is upon you, appoint scribes and [?] to judge all the people beyond the River and all those who know the law of God. Teach those who do not know it.
Anyone who does not obey the law of God and the law of the king shall be judged immediately, whether sentenced to death, confiscation of property, flogging, or forced labor.
Ezra said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put it into the king’s heart to honor his house in Jerusalem.”
Some of the people of Israel, and some of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of the reign of King Artaxerxes.
These are the heads of their ancestral families who were listed to go up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
Hashabiah and Jeshaiah, from the descendants of Merari, together with his brothers and sons, were twenty.
From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; from the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel; and from the descendants of David, Hattush.
We fasted and prayed to our God about this, and he heard us.
I weighed out for them the gold, silver, and vessels for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all the Israelites who were there had previously sent.
I weighed them out into their hands and gave them six hundred and fifty talents of silver, one hundred talents of gold, and one hundred silver vessels.

On the fourth day we weighed all the gold, silver, and vessels in the house of our God and entrusted them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad son of Joses and Noadiah son of Binnui, who were Levites.
I gave the king’s letter to the king’s administrators and to the officials beyond the River, and they honored the people and the house of the Lord.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
From the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
And now, Lord, what shall we say? While you give to them, they have disobeyed your commandment.
He took a wife from among their daughters, and they married off their sons. The holy offspring mingled with the people of the land, and the officials were the first to join them in this sin.

From the days of our fathers until today we have been greatly guilty. Because of our sins, we, our kings, our priests, and our children were taken captive and fell into the hands of the kings of the nations. They killed us with their swords, took us captive, and plundered us, and we remain ashamed to this day.
And God called the dry land Earth, and he called the gathered waters Sea. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening, and morning came, and it was the third day.
And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night, together with its stars.
